claims.nodeLabel: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
claims.text: Recommendation 1: 'We recommend that the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, in coordination with the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office Director, issue a Department of Defense policy to integrate unidentified anomalous phenomena roles, responsibilities, requirements, and coordination procedures into existing intelligence, counterintelligence, and force protection policies and procedures. The policy should include methods to address unidentified anomalous phenomena incidents and should align with policies and procedures for the protection of United States persons' civil liberties.' USD(I&S) and the AARO Director agreed; the recommendation was left 'resolved but open'.

claims.nodeLabel: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
claims.text: The classified evaluation is Report No. DODIG-2023-109, 'Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena,' dated August 15, 2023. A 16-page unclassified summary was published January 24-25, 2024; it carries the note: 'A classified version of the Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena formed the basis of the unclassified summary.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
claims.text: On the absence of a response plan: 'The DoD has not issued a comprehensive UAP response plan that identifies roles, responsibilities, requirements, and coordination procedures... As a result, the DoD response to UAP incidents is uncoordinated and concentrated within each Military Department. Officials from the Military Services and MDCOs stated that they have been waiting for the DoD to issue comprehensive UAP guidance before developing their own guidance.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
claims.text: Consequence finding: 'We determined that the DoD has no overarching UAP policy and, as a result, it lacks assurance that national security and flight safety threats to the United States from UAP have been identified and mitigated.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
claims.sourceText: https://media.defense.gov/2024/Jan/25/2003381266/-1/-1/1/UNCLASSIFIED%20SUMMARY_UNIDENTIFIED%20ANOMALOUS%20PHENOMENA%20SECURE.PDF — DEMOTED from Tier 1 (sourced to an interested party (AARO/DoD) asserting an external fact; primary record of the statement, not of the fact); needs primary replacement
claims.text: Historical framing in the summary: 'Over the past decades, the DoD has initiated infrequent and inconclusive efforts to identify and understand the origin, capabilities, and intent of unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP)... the DoD has relied heavily on the Services and Components to detect, report, collect, analyze, and identify UAP since the 1940s.' It counts 243 sightings investigated under PROJECT SIGN (1947-1949) and 'over 12,000 reported sightings' under PROJECT BLUE BOOK (1952-1969).

claims.text: Core finding, 'The DoD Does Not Have a Comprehensive, Coordinated Approach to Address UAP': 'the DoD has not used a coordinated approach to detect, report, collect, analyze, and identify UAP; DoD Components have largely excluded geographic combatant commands... in developing UAP policies and procedures; and DoD Components developed varying processes to collect, analyze, and identify UAP incidents.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
claims.text: The IG's finding that DoD had no overarching UAP policy and 'lacks assurance' that threats were identified or mitigated is a primary-record statement of institutional incapacity, not of concealment; it is nonetheless the strongest official acknowledgment on the record that DoD's UAP handling was uncoordinated across the very period in which AARO was assuring Congress the historical record was fully reviewed. Reasoning: the IG evaluation (Aug 2023) and HRR Vol I (Feb 2024) overlap in period and subject but reach differently scoped conclusions.

a.label: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)

edges.label: The IG found no department-wide UAP policy and component-level stovepipes
edges.note: Eighteen months after AARO was made the Department's authoritative UAP office, the Inspector General found no requirement that components report to it - which makes AARO's holdings a self-selected sample.

edges.label: NDAs and IG channels bound what a witness may say
edges.note: DODIG-2023-109 exists because personnel used the Inspector General channel; the legal domain determines which disclosures are protected and which are prosecutable.

b.label: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)

edges.label: the data-sharing streamlining provision answers the IG's 2023 reporting-requirement finding
edges.note: The IG found components were not required to report to AARO; two years later Congress legislated to streamline agency data sharing into AARO investigations.
